raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year. I been farming this same land for more than fifty years, so I already know what I'm doing. My son helps when he can but he works in town part of the time. My wife is still able to help in the field, and the grandkids help some during busy times like when we bring in the wheat or the maize.

Thirty mu is not a small plot but it's not big either. I manage most of it myself with family, and I hire a tractor and combine when I need them — no point in owning machines at my age. I always do wheat-maize, same as everyone in the village. You can't eat if you only plant one crop. And the land here is flat with good groundwater, so it works.

**For the wheat this fall (planted last October, coming to harvest now in June):**

I always plant in early-mid October right after I clear the maize stalks. I used the Jimai variety again, bought some new seed from the agri-store, about 15 kg per mu, a bit thick because the weather was dry when I planted. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer — I use the 15-15-15 kind, about 40 kg per mu, and a bit of urea mixed in. That's what I always do, my neighbors do the same.

I watered the wheat over winter (winter water is important, old farmers always say "winter water is gold"), then again in spring around jointing time I topdressed urea, maybe 15 kg per mu, and watered again. That was in March. If it doesn't rain enough before harvest I'll water once more at the grain-filling stage. The pumping costs money — each watering is maybe 40 yuan per mu with the well — but without water the yield drops a lot and I learned that lesson long ago.

For pests, I sprayed once against aphids and rust when I saw them in the spring. Nothing fancy, the stuff the shop sells.

I'm hoping for around 450 kg per mu. Last year I got about 470, year before was a bit less because of dry spring. It depends on the weather in the last month.

**For the maize going in after wheat harvest (mid-June planting):**

As soon as I cut the wheat I need to get the maize in — no time to waste, every day matters for maize, the growing season is short. I'll hire the combine for wheat and then the maize planter right after. No deep plowing, just direct seed into the stubble — everyone does it this way now, saves time and the roots do fine.

For maize I always buy hybrid seed, you can't save it like wheat. Zhengdan or Denghai varieties, whatever the shop has that the neighbors say is good. Maybe 60-70 yuan per mu for seed.

I put compound fertilizer at planting, about 30-40 kg per mu of 15-15-15, and then when the maize gets to about knee-high (big trumpet stage) I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu. That's how I've always done it, gives about 14-15 kg of nitrogen per mu total I suppose.

For water — it depends on the rain. Usually summer rains come and I may only need to water once or twice. If it's a dry summer I water more. The maize needs water most at tasseling and grain-filling, I watch for that.

Pests — usually some armyworm or corn borer, I spray once if I see them. Weeds I spray herbicide right after planting.

Yield I'm hoping 500 kg per mu, maybe more if the summer is good. I got 520 last year. My neighbor with the same size farm got about 550, but his seed is a bit fancier.

**Labor and money:**

Most of the work my wife and I do ourselves, with help from my son when he's not in town. For harvest and planting I hire machines, not workers — that costs maybe 50-80 yuan per mu for combine, 30 yuan for planter. I pay cash.

I don't have big money to spare so I buy fertilizer when I have the cash after selling grain. I never borrow — I don't like owing money at my age. If a year is bad I eat less and we manage.
